classification.method: fixed host: every load is a new process (cold); no restore exists; warm = the same process's later requests

conclusion: FIXED HOST, NOT LAMBDA. 0xd40 local-file: load -2.031 s (5/5), peak RSS -488 MB; memfd -2.028 s, -471 MB; warm/forward no change; answers bit-identical (50/50, 10/10). x86_64: peak RSS -575 MB (5/5, outside 1% floor); timings no change inside the noisy co-tenanted host's spread; answers identical to x86 P1. Dormant: no change. No path degrades, but the switch aborts any request for logits, so it is only valid for engines that never ask for them (decshim). Verdict: general opt-in, default ON inside decshim-only deployments; not a llama.cpp-wide default.

conditions.note: FIXED HOST, NOT LAMBDA LATENCY. One fresh container per load; arms interleaved by cyclic rotation of one round's order; comparisons pair rounds (arm minus p1 in the same round).

cost.note: fixed host already provisioned; no AWS calls

functions.note: memory_mb is P1's Lambda setting, kept for the schema; the container has no memory limit (cgroup memory.max as recorded per load)

hypothesis: Skipping the tied output head (LKAI_SKIP_TIED_OUTPUT=1) saves its repack time and memory on every decshim deployment.
reproduce: python3 general/summarize.py <arm64 run> <x86 run> <x86 e6 run> --out <dir> --verdicts general/verdicts.json --commit <ladder sha> --run-id <id>
